context:
An Agent Workflows workflow was started in detached mode to audit a large repository. The user left it running overnight. In the morning, `agent-workflows ps` shows:

```txt
RUN ID        STATE     PHASE      AGENTS  UPDATED
run_8241      running   Verify     18/20   2026-06-24T01:12:44Z
```

`agent-workflows watch run_8241 --tail 80` ends with:

```txt
[Analyze] eval:api-13 completed schema-valid
[Analyze] eval:ui-14 completed schema-valid
[Verify] eval:security-17 retry 1 schema validation failed: missing confidence
[Verify] eval:security-17 retry 2 schema validation failed: missing confidence
[Verify] eval:security-17 retry 3 schema validation failed: missing confidence
[Verify] eval:security-17 failed: retry limit exceeded
[Verify] eval:release-18 running for 5h21m; last output 5h19m ago
[run] admission paused after failure; completed results retained in journal
```

`status.json` says the run has `state: "running"`, `admission: "paused"`, one failed agent, one running agent, and 18 completed agents. `result.json` does not exist. `journal.json` exists and is 14 MB. The user wants the final report today, but does not want to re-run the completed repository analysis if avoidable. The machine is online now. You may assume the CLI supports `agent-workflows control <runId> stop-agent <agentId>`, `resume-admission`, `stop-run`, and `agent-workflows resume <runId>`.
task: Decide how to recover this long-running workflow run with minimal lost work. Explain what happened, what to inspect next, and the safest resume or control sequence.
title: Detached Workflow Run Recovery
